item.title: Recording Academy Discussing Future of New Asian Pop Category
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to our podcast, where we dive into the latest music news. Today, we're talking about the Grammys and their new category, Best Asian Pop Music Performance. But it seems not everyone is happy about it.
[Soft music continues in the background]
Host: The Recording Academy announced the new category on June 16, but K-pop sensation BTS has decided not to submit their music for consideration this year. In a statement, the group expressed their desire for music to be judged on its own merit, rather than being divided by region or language.
[Music transitions to a slight pause]
Host: The Recording Academy's CEO, Harvey Mason, Jr., has been in talks with members of the Asian pop community, including K-pop, J-pop, and C-pop representatives. The goal is to ensure the new category honors the music respectfully and accurately. Mason stated that the Grammy organization exists to serve all music people and wants to make sure no voice or community is overlooked or misunderstood.
[Music picks up slightly]
Host: As a result of the backlash, the Academy is re-evaluating its process for creating new categories. They're considering making the process more transparent and open, rather than keeping it confidential. This could mean losing the element of surprise when new categories are announced, but it could also lead to more inclusive and representative categories.
[Music transitions to a calm tone]
Host: The Academy's full Board and Awards & Nominations Committee will work with the Asian pop community to advise on the new category and determine how to best honor this music in the future. It's a step towards greater inclusivity and understanding in the music industry.
[Outro music plays]
Host: That's all for today. Thanks for tuning in to our podcast. We'll keep you updated on the latest music news and developments.
